# Explained corpus changes

Every change of a corpus golden (`corpus/goldens/<id>.edges`) is explained here, one entry per changed reference, before the golden is rewritten. `npm run corpus` fails on any change no entry explains, and `npm run corpus:update` refuses to rewrite a golden while one is unexplained. The oracles (`npm run corpus:oracles`) read the same file: a disagreement with a language's own resolver is explained the same way when it is a known limit or a limit of the oracle.

An entry is a list item of exactly one of these forms, the first for an edge change and the second for an oracle disagreement:

```
- `<repository>` `<kind>` `<from>:<line>` `<target>`: <reason>
- `<repository>` `<kind>` `<from>:<line>` `<subject>` `<Runes' answer>` `<the oracle's answer>`: <reason>
```

- The repository, `<repository>`, is an id of `corpus/manifest.json`.
- The kind, `<kind>`, is `+` for a reference the golden lacks, `-` for a reference of the golden that is gone, or `<oracle>:<disagreement>` for an oracle (`typescript:false-edge`, `typescript:recall-loss`, `typescript:mismatch`, `python:false-edge`, `cargo:mismatch`, `cargo:crlf`, `go:false-edge`, `go:recall-loss`, `go:mismatch`, `csharp:recall-loss`, `csharp:false-reach`, `c:false-edge`, `c:unreadable`). Any other kind is refused.
- The site, `<from>:<line>`, is the referencing file and line; `*` for the line explains every line of that file with that kind, target and answers. Use it only where every such line has the same cause.
- The target, `<target>`, is the file the reference resolves to; for an oracle, the subject, `<subject>`, is the specifier, the field, or the project the disagreement is about.
- An oracle entry then names both answers it explains: what Runes answered and what the oracle answered, as the oracle run prints them (`silent` where Runes binds nothing, `unresolved in the repository` where TypeScript finds no tracked file; for `cargo:crlf`, the LF reading and the CRLF reading). The entry stops matching the moment either answer changes, so an explanation cannot go on covering a site after Runes, or the oracle, moves to another answer. The run prints every unexplained disagreement in this form, without the reason, and names the entries of an oracle that ran and matched nothing.
- The reason says why: the change that made it, named by its commit or merge on the branch that carries it, or why the difference is right.

A list item that opens with a backtick and does not read this way, names a repository the manifest does not hold, or names a kind no comparison reports, fails the run with its line, so a mistyped entry cannot explain nothing in silence. A change that touches the edges of a language regenerates the goldens of the corpus repositories in that language in the same commit (`npm run corpus:update -- --only <id>`) and adds its entries under a heading of its own. Two changes that touch one golden are reconciled by regenerating it on the merged tip and keeping both sets of entries.

## From 1.0.0 to release 1.1.0

The goldens were made with the `v1.0.0` tag's `dist/` and then with each first-parent merge of `release/1.1.0` in turn, and each changed reference is attributed to the merge after which it last changed. A merge's subject names the work it carries. Removed references: 21 in google-cloud-python and 12 in poetry, all standard-library imports (`import logging`, `import json`) that bound to a same-named directory of the repository; 387 in react and 6 in jest, bare names that bound to a package.json no workspace declares (react's compiler playground imports `react` from its own dependencies, not from `packages/react`). No other reference of 1.0.0 is gone.

### Merge f2ad16b

Changed: C#: the directive line of a plain using alias inside a namespace body reads its target in the nearest namespace only, so an alias whose target lies farther out gives no edge on that line; every line that uses the alias keeps its edge (ruling csharp-unused-alias-silence-over-false-edge of the Althing 6.2.0 loop).

- `eShop` `-` `tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/OrdersWebApiTest.cs:5` `src/Ordering.API/Application/Queries/OrderViewModel.cs`: merge f2ad16b; the alias `Order` is used on lines 110, 119 and 120 of the same file, which keep their edges to the same target

### Merge 6d01d91 (commit 2a26e66)

Changed: C#: a plain using directive inside a namespace body is read at that namespace, before the next namespace outward and before the global usings of the project, and only inside its own block. In eShop each such using sits below a file-scoped namespace and imports a type that a global using of the project also brings under the same name, so the file's own using now decides, as it does in C#.

### Merge 6d01d91 (commit 83b0dea)

Changed: C#: the directive line of a plain using alias inside a namespace body reads every reading of its target again, each farther one behind the nearer namespaces or types of its first segment, so a fully qualified target whose first segment names nothing nearer in the repository gives its edge. This restores the reference merge f2ad16b removed.

- `eShop` `+` `tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/OrdersWebApiTest.cs:5` `src/Ordering.API/Application/Queries/OrderViewModel.cs`: the commit "csharp: a fully qualified alias target gives its directive edge when nothing nearer has its first name"; `using Order = eShop.Ordering.API.Application.Queries.Order;` below `namespace eShop.Ordering.UnitTests.Application;`, and the repository declares no namespace or type `eShop` nearer than the global one

### Merge ce1f552 (commit 86ca136)

Fixed: a file that several referenced tsconfig projects include takes the `paths` of the first one in the order of `references`, where Runes had stayed silent when the projects disagreed.

- `airflow` `+` `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/tests/e2e/fixtures/asset-data.ts:22` `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/tests/e2e/fixtures/index.ts`: the first referenced tsconfig that includes a file serves it, so the `tests/*` and `*` paths of the UI tsconfig.app.json bind the import (tsserver takes the first project in the order of `references`, and tests/** is included by tsconfig.app.json before tsconfig.dev.json)

### Merge 5a644bb (commit 63a57bc)

Fixed: C#: an extension-method call reads the static classes of the global namespace before the namespaces the compilation unit's using directives import, as C# does. A global static class declaring the called method now wins over an imported one. Where several projects declare such a global method and the reference graph cannot rule them out, the call is ambiguous and gives no edge.

### Merge 7e1cd3a (commit d680c05)

Fixed: an import of a package whose `exports` lists conditions binds the target TypeScript chooses by the conditions of the importing file's settings (`import` or `require` by its module format, `types`, `node` except under Bundler, and its `customConditions`), where Runes took the first target that named a file. Each line below was a tracked oracle false edge, and its oracle line leaves the section below.

### Merge 7e1cd3a (commit 39a3b3b)

Fixed: a workspace package declared by a version range or a tag binds only where the package manager, read from the root's `packageManager` or its lockfile, links it (npm and yarn for a satisfied range, pnpm only with `link-workspace-packages` on), where Runes bound any workspace package of that name. In react every such reference is a fixture that pins an older or experimental React.

- `react` `-` `fixtures/attribute-behavior/src/App.js:1` `packages/react/react.react-server.js`: the commit "typescript: a workspace package declared by a range binds only where the package manager links it"; the fixture declares `react` as `^15.6.1`, which the workspace package at 19.3.0 does not satisfy, and the repository names yarn 1.22.22 as its package manager, which links a workspace package only for a range its version satisfies (never for a tag), so the fixture gets a registry copy of `react`

### Commit "csharp: a simple name reads the nested types of its enclosing types first"

Fixed: C#: a simple name written inside a type reads the nested types of each enclosing type, from every part of a partial type, before any namespace, alias or using, as C# does. A nested `SearchResult` no longer gives an edge to an imported `SearchResult`.

- `jellyfin` `-` `MediaBrowser.Providers/Plugins/Omdb/OmdbItemProvider.cs:155` `MediaBrowser.Controller/Library/SearchResult.cs`: the commit "csharp: a simple name reads the nested types of its enclosing types first"; `OmdbItemProvider` nests a private class `SearchResult`, and C# reads the nested types of the enclosing type before the `using MediaBrowser.Controller.Library;` that imports another `SearchResult`, so the reference names the nested class of its own file; this was a false edge
- `jellyfin` `-` `MediaBrowser.Providers/Plugins/Omdb/OmdbItemProvider.cs:180` `MediaBrowser.Controller/Library/SearchResult.cs`: the commit "csharp: a simple name reads the nested types of its enclosing types first"; `OmdbItemProvider` nests a private class `SearchResult`, and C# reads the nested types of the enclosing type before the `using MediaBrowser.Controller.Library;` that imports another `SearchResult`, so the reference names the nested class of its own file; this was a false edge
- `jellyfin` `-` `MediaBrowser.Providers/Plugins/Omdb/OmdbItemProvider.cs:308` `MediaBrowser.Controller/Library/SearchResult.cs`: the commit "csharp: a simple name reads the nested types of its enclosing types first"; `OmdbItemProvider` nests a private class `SearchResult`, and C# reads the nested types of the enclosing type before the `using MediaBrowser.Controller.Library;` that imports another `SearchResult`, so the reference names the nested class of its own file; this was a false edge

### Commit "csharp: the generic arity takes part in the lookup"

Fixed: C#: a type name with type arguments binds only a type with that many type parameters, and a bare name only a non-generic type, as C# does. `Result<int>` no longer binds a nearer non-generic `Result`, and `Result` and `Result<T>` declared in two components each keep their edge.

- `jellyfin` `+` `Emby.Server.Implementations/HttpServer/WebSocketConnection.cs:109` `MediaBrowser.Controller/Net/WebSocketMessages/OutboundWebSocketMessageOfT.cs`: the commit "csharp: the generic arity takes part in the lookup"; the reference is written with type arguments and names the generic type the target file declares; without arity that type and the non-generic type of the same name, in the same directory, declared one key and the lookup took the non-generic one, so only the file changes, not the owner

### Commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"

Fixed: C#: a `Compile` item that links a file from outside the project's directory adds that file to the project and nothing else, so a project that compiles a shared file no longer counts as seeing every project, and neither does every project that references it. An internal type or extension class of a referenced project is no longer a candidate unless that project names the caller as a friend (`InternalsVisibleTo`).

- `eShop` `+` `src/Basket.API/Program.cs:4` `src/Basket.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `builder.AddApplicationServices()` reads the global namespace first, where Catalog.API, Ordering.API, Webhooks.API and WebApp each declare a global `AddApplicationServices`; Basket.API references EventBusRabbitMQ, whose linked `..\Shared\ActivityExtensions.cs` no longer opens the reference graph, so the global methods of projects Basket.API does not reference are out of reach, and the call binds Basket.API's own method through its global using, as the compiler does; this edge was lost to that open graph
- `eShop` `+` `src/Catalog.API/Program.cs:6` `src/Catalog.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `builder.AddApplicationServices()` reads the global namespace first, where Catalog.API, Ordering.API, Webhooks.API and WebApp each declare a global `AddApplicationServices`; Catalog.API references EventBusRabbitMQ, whose linked `..\Shared\ActivityExtensions.cs` no longer opens the reference graph, so the global methods of projects Catalog.API does not reference are out of reach, and the call binds Catalog.API's own global method, as the compiler does
- `eShop` `+` `src/OrderProcessor/Program.cs:4` `src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `builder.AddApplicationServices()` reads the global namespace first, where Catalog.API, Ordering.API, Webhooks.API and WebApp each declare a global `AddApplicationServices`; OrderProcessor references EventBusRabbitMQ, whose linked `..\Shared\ActivityExtensions.cs` no longer opens the reference graph, so the global methods of projects OrderProcessor does not reference are out of reach, and the call binds OrderProcessor's own method through its global using, as the compiler does; this edge was lost to that open graph
- `eShop` `+` `src/Ordering.API/Program.cs:4` `src/Ordering.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `builder.AddApplicationServices()` reads the global namespace first, where Catalog.API, Ordering.API, Webhooks.API and WebApp each declare a global `AddApplicationServices`; Ordering.API references EventBusRabbitMQ, whose linked `..\Shared\ActivityExtensions.cs` no longer opens the reference graph, so the global methods of projects Ordering.API does not reference are out of reach, and the call binds Ordering.API's own internal method, as the compiler does
- `eShop` `+` `src/WebApp/Program.cs:10` `src/WebApp/Extensions/Extensions.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `builder.AddApplicationServices()` reads the global namespace, where Catalog.API, Ordering.API, Webhooks.API and WebApp each declare a global `AddApplicationServices`; WebApp references none of the other three, and the projects it references no longer reach everything through EventBusRabbitMQ's linked file, so the call binds WebApp's own method, as the compiler does
- `eShop` `+` `src/Webhooks.API/Program.cs:4` `src/Webhooks.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `builder.AddApplicationServices()` reads the global namespace first, where Catalog.API, Ordering.API, Webhooks.API and WebApp each declare a global `AddApplicationServices`; Webhooks.API references EventBusRabbitMQ, whose linked `..\Shared\ActivityExtensions.cs` no longer opens the reference graph, so the global methods of projects Webhooks.API does not reference are out of reach, and the call binds Webhooks.API's own internal method, as the compiler does
- `eShop` `+` `tests/Catalog.FunctionalTests/CatalogApiFixture.cs:10` `src/Catalog.API/Program.Testing.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` names the global `Program`, which Catalog.API and Ordering.API each declare as `public partial class Program { }`; Catalog.FunctionalTests references Catalog.API only, and the graph no longer reaches everything through EventBusRabbitMQ's linked file, so Ordering.API's class is out of reach and the reference binds Catalog.API's, as the compiler does
- `eShop` `+` `tests/Catalog.FunctionalTests/CatalogApiTests.cs:15` `src/Catalog.API/Program.Testing.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; the same `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`, the same two declared classes and the same closed graph: Catalog.API's class
- `eShop` `+` `tests/Webhooks.FunctionalTests/WebhooksApiFixture.cs:8` `src/Webhooks.API/Program.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` names the global `Program`; Webhooks.FunctionalTests references Webhooks.API only, and with the graph no longer open through EventBusRabbitMQ's linked file the declared classes of Catalog.API and Ordering.API are out of reach, so the reference binds the class the compiler makes of Webhooks.API's top-level statements, as the compiler does
- `jellyfin` `-` `tests/Jellyfin.Server.Integration.Tests/JellyfinApplicationFactory.cs:91` `Jellyfin.Server/Program.cs`: the commit "csharp: a linked file belongs only to the projects that link it, and an internal declaration is seen only by its own project and its friends"; the chained `.ConfigureAppConfiguration((context, builder) => …)` on the web host builder is ASP.NET's method, and the only in-repository definer, `Jellyfin.Server.Program`, declares its `ConfigureAppConfiguration(this IConfigurationBuilder …)` as `private`, which no other assembly can call; Jellyfin.Server names only Jellyfin.Server.Tests as a friend, so the method is no candidate for the integration tests; this was a false edge

### Commit "typescript: a file no tsconfig covers reads exports with the default conditions, a require() or import() call reads its own, and a versioned types key is entered by the compiler's version"

Fixed: an import in a file no tsconfig covers binds the target Node and TypeScript choose from a package's `exports` (`import` or `require` by the file's format, `types`, `node` and `default`), where Runes took the first target that named a file, so `react`, `react-dom/server` and the other React packages no longer bind their `react-server`, edge or native builds; and a dynamic `import()` reads the `import` condition, so koa's own test no longer binds the `require` target of `koa` (the `import` target is build output). Each pair of lines below is one import: the target of the golden and the one it now has.

- `react` `-` `fixtures/art/VectorWidget.js:10` `packages/react/react.react-server.js`: the commit "typescript: a file no tsconfig covers reads exports with the default conditions, a require() or import() call reads its own, and a versioned types key is entered by the compiler's version"; `react-server`, a condition of React's server rendering that neither Node nor TypeScript enters by default, is listed before `default`, so a file no tsconfig covers binds the `default` target.
- `react` `+` `fixtures/art/VectorWidget.js:10` `packages/react/index.js`: the commit "typescript: a file no tsconfig covers reads exports with the default conditions, a require() or import() call reads its own, and a versioned types key is entered by the compiler's version"; the same import, now bound to the target Node and TypeScript choose: `react-server`, a condition of React's server rendering that neither Node nor TypeScript enters by default, is listed before `default`, so a file no tsconfig covers binds the `default` target.

### Commit "typescript: a package entry under outDir that is not in the repository maps back to its source"

Added: an import of a workspace package whose `exports`, `types` or `main` names build output that the commit does not hold binds the source the output is compiled from, read through the package's own tsconfig (`outDir` back to `rootDir`). In jest every package names `./build/` and sets `rootDir` `src` and `outDir` `build`; next-intl's `types` name `dist/types/`, which its `tsconfig.build.json` writes from `src`; ky's `tsconfig.dist.json` writes `distribution/` from `source`; zod and react have a few packages of the same shape. No reference is removed.

### Branch jarl/494-csharp-base-classes (commits a46bd83, 5839ee0, 318eaa7, 63e9cd8 and those after them)

C#: base lists are recorded, so an extension call gives way to an instance method of the receiver's written type, and a member a class inherits or another part declares is a value. Only jellyfin moves; CleanArchitecture and eShop keep every reference. Of jellyfin's references this branch adds 15 and removes 176; 12 of the removed ones are true references lost to the known limit named in their entries.

- `jellyfin` `+` `Jellyfin.Server.Implementations/Item/BaseItemRepository.TranslateQuery.cs:*` `src/Jellyfin.Extensions/EnumerableExtensions.cs`: commit 63e9cd8: the receiver is a field another part of the partial class declares, so the call now reads as an extension call, as it does when the file itself declares the field. The extension of that name in scope takes other arguments: an extension key carries no parameter shape, a known limit that held for a field of the same file before
- `jellyfin` `+` `MediaBrowser.Controller/Entities/Audio/MusicArtist.cs:*` `src/Jellyfin.Extensions/GuidExtensions.cs`: commit 63e9cd8: the receiver is a member the class inherits from a base class of the repository, or that another part of it declares: a value, so the call binds the extension method in scope

### Commit "csharp: an extension method takes a call only when it can take the number of its arguments"

Removed: C#: a call whose reading binds one owner of an extension method of that name, where no extension method of that name the owner declares can take the number of arguments (or of written type arguments) the call passes. The method each of these calls binds is an instance method or an extension method from outside the repository (`Sessions.FirstOrDefault(i => …)` is LINQ's, beside a `FirstOrDefault<T>(this IReadOnlyList<T>)` without a parameter; `ids.Contains(id)` beside a `Contains(this IEnumerable<string>, ReadOnlySpan<char>, StringComparison)`; `text.Split('_', 2)` beside a `Split(this ReadOnlySpan<char>, char)`). No reference is added: a name two owners declare at one level stays ambiguous, whatever their shapes.

### Commit "typescript: an exports pattern target is taken as written, with no extension added (issue 646)"

Removed: TypeScript: an `exports` pattern target written without an extension names that path and no `.js` file beside it.

- `react` `-` `packages/react-client/src/ReactFlightClient.js:116` `packages/react/src/ReactSharedInternalsServer.js`: the commit "typescript: an exports pattern target is taken as written, with no extension added (issue 646)"; the package's `exports` map `./src/*` to `./src/*` and the import names no extension, so the target is a path with no file of that name; Node and TypeScript take an `exports` target as it is written and resolve nothing, and Runes no longer probes it as it probes a path, so it no longer binds the `.js` file beside it (the file Flow and the repository's own build read for this import); this was a false edge

### Commit "csharp: a member access compared with or assigned to a value of the type of its own name gives the edge to that type (issue 747)"

Added: C#: `Status == Status.Active` and `Status = Status.Done`, where the file also declares a value `Status` of the type `Status` (a property, a field, a typed, `var` or lambda-inferred local or parameter), give the edge to the type `Status`: C# reads the static member through the type (spec §12.8.7.2). jellyfin gains 35 references and eShop 14; each is an enum member read beside a property of that enum's type and its own name, and none is gone.

## Oracle disagreements at release 1.1.0

What the oracles report (`npm run corpus`, or `npm run corpus:oracles` alone) on the tip of `release/1.1.0` that is a known limit of Runes, a choice Runes makes on purpose, or a limit of the oracle itself, for both tiers. A disagreement where Runes is wrong and no change of Runes has yet answered it is not explained here: it keeps the gate red until Runes changes. On the heavy tier that is, at the pinned commits, jellyfin's two fuzz projects (Runes carries the reach of an assembly reference on to the references of the project that builds the assembly, which the compiler never sees).

The heavy tier below was read by hand at the pinned commits. Its TypeScript entries share one limit of the oracle: it links into `node_modules` the workspaces of the repository root alone, so a nested project with its own lockfile and workspaces (react's `compiler/`, its fixtures) is resolved as if the root's install served it.
